title: Research
text: How does the developing visual cortex arrive at reliable representations of the outside world? Before eye opening, cortical networks already show structured spontaneous activity. After eye opening, visual experience reshapes this endogenous activity into representations that respond consistently to the same stimulus. My research asks which circuit mechanisms carry this transition.

title: Research
text:
Emergence of reliable cortical representations
At eye opening, responses of ferret visual cortex to the same stimulus vary strongly from trial to trial. Over the following days they become reliable. Combining chronic two-photon imaging with recurrent network models, we found that this reliability arises when visual input becomes aligned with the endogenous network structure, rather than from a general reduction of noise. See Trägenap et al., Nature Neuroscience 2025 (press release · free-to-read version).

title: Research
text:
Feedforward input and recurrent circuits
How do feedforward inputs interact with recurrent cortical circuits during development? Together with the Fitzpatrick lab we showed that coherent cortical responses develop as feedforward inputs become more discriminable and better aligned with the recurrent network. See Lempel, Trägenap et al., Neuron 2025 (press release · doi:10.1016/j.neuron.2025.08.014).

title: Research
text:
Millimetre-scale selective amplification
With the Smith lab we study how the developing cortex selectively amplifies particular activity patterns across millimetres of cortical surface, and which recurrent subnetworks can account for this. See Mulholland, Trägenap et al., bioRxiv 2026 (co-first authors; doi:10.64898/2026.03.31.715687).

title: Outreach
text:
Interactive exhibit: EEG Mindball
Together with Bettina Hein, a former PhD student in our lab, I developed an EEG Mindball, an interactive exhibit in which visitors try to move a ball by generating a certain signal in their recorded EEG data. It is based on an exhibit at the phaeno science centre in Wolfsburg and serves as a hands-on introduction to brain signals. It has been used at various events, such as the Hessen schafft Wissen exhibitions (for example at the Frankfurt Book Fair), the FIAS 20-year anniversary, the Night of Science, and the FIAS booth at Frankfurt hat Hirn 2024.

title: Sigrid Trägenap
text:
I am a computational neuroscientist at the Frankfurt Institute for Advanced Studies (FIAS) and Goethe University Frankfurt, in the group of Matthias Kaschube.
I study how reliable sensory representations emerge during the development of the visual cortex, combining recurrent network models with chronic imaging data from ferret visual cortex. I submitted my PhD thesis in January 2026.
